problem.passage:
Text 1

Art historians examining the sudden popularity of chiaroscuro—the dramatic use of light and shadow—in seventeenth-century European painting often attribute the technique's rise to the influence of a small circle of innovative painters whose bold canvases circulated among wealthy patrons in major cities. According to this view, once influential collectors began commissioning works featuring stark contrasts of illumination, provincial painters imitated the style to attract similarly prestigious clients, and the technique spread outward from urban centers of artistic patronage to the wider continent within a few decades.

Text 2

The patronage-driven account of chiaroscuro's spread overlooks a simpler explanation rooted in materials rather than taste. Analysis of surviving pigments and canvases shows that this same period saw the wider availability of more affordable, stable dark pigments capable of rendering deep shadow without cracking or fading, alongside improved oil-based mediums that allowed for more precise gradations of light. Painters in provincial workshops, far from imitating fashionable urban patrons, appear to have adopted these techniques largely because the newly available materials simply made dramatic light effects easier and cheaper to produce reliably, regardless of who was commissioning the work.

Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to Text 1's explanation that chiaroscuro spread because provincial painters imitated urban patrons' tastes?

problem.question: Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to Text 1's explanation that chiaroscuro spread because provincial painters imitated urban patrons' tastes?
options: The author would agree that patron taste was the decisive factor, while adding that material improvements played only a minor supporting role in the process.

The author would contend that provincial painters adopted dramatic light and shadow effects because newly affordable, stable pigments and mediums made the technique easier to produce, not because they were imitating urban patrons.

The author would maintain that both explanations are equally valid, since material advances and patrons' preference for the new style emerged together and reinforced one another in spreading the technique.
The author would claim that wealthy urban patrons rejected chiaroscuro and that only provincial painters embraced it independently of any material changes.
problem.explanation: Text 1은 부유한 후원자들의 취향을 모방하여 치오스쿠로가 도시에서 지방으로 확산되었다고 설명한다. Text 2는 이 시기에 안정적인 어두운 안료와 개선된 유화 매체가 더 저렴하게 보급되었다는 점을 근거로, 지방 화가들이 후원자를 모방한 것이 아니라 재료 자체가 극적인 명암 효과를 쉽고 싸게 만들었기 때문에 이 기법을 채택했다고 반박한다. 따라서 정답은 B번이다.
problem.evidenceTarget: Text 2는 Text 1이 제시한 '지방 화가의 후원자 취향 모방' 설명을 재료(안료·매체)의 보급이라는 대안적 원인으로 반박한다.
problem.evidenceSpan: Painters in provincial workshops, far from imitating fashionable urban patrons, appear to have adopted these techniques largely because the newly available materials simply made dramatic light effects easier and cheaper to produce reliably, regardless of who was commissioning the work.
problem.answerRationale: Text 2가 명시한 재료 요인(안정적 안료, 개선된 매체)이 후원자 모방 설명을 대체한다고 직접 진술하므로, 이 인과관계를 그대로 반영한 선택지가 정답이다.
